fatal_flaws.claim: "A_D = P_T(Σ_{k∈D∪{0,0′}} G̃_k)P_T". Channel Fisher operators are added as if the channels were independent observations. Plug-in ΔV̂ is the screen, and KG and the posterior P(γ>3pp) are built on A_D.
fatal_flaws.problem: Every rubric channel is computed on the same trajectory as won. Channel 0′ (sign of G−G′) is also computed from that trajectory, and it correlates 0.79–0.89 with won. Adding the information matrices counts the same evidence twice. As a result, near-copies of the outcome get the largest ΔV̂: 'completed' (P(won|completed) 0.81–0.90), sign(G), and 'ran out of steps'. The screen then fills its top 8 with these copies. The cross-fit confirm step correctly gives them about 0, so the screen and the confirm step disagree by construction. KG allocation and the model posterior are overconfident too, which pushes the wrong-keep rate above nominal. §8 notices the problem ('use a sandwich') but only for the screen, not for A_D itself.
fatal_flaws.fix: Define the information of channel j for each pair from the joint model of the channel vector. G̃_{j|0} is the Schur complement of the joint per-pair Fisher matrix of (z_0, z_0′, z_D, z_j) against the channels already present. Equivalently, it is the information in z_j conditional on the gold channels of the same pair. If z_j is a deterministic function of z_0, its information is 0. Build A_D, H_c and KG from this conditional information.

fatal_flaws.claim: "With π ≡ 1 the rubric adds exactly nothing (Kallus & Mao, Cor. 2.1)". Also: "To first order this [ρ_j] is the AoS information increment ΔV_{c,j}". Also P1: ΔV=0 iff B_jH_c=0.
fatal_flaws.problem: These are two different estimands, and they contradict each other. ΔV in P1 is a model-based efficiency gain under a restricted low-rank model. It is strictly positive at π≡1 whenever B_jH_c≠0, because auxiliary channels that share factors sharpen u_c. ρ_j is the reduction in the design variance of the AIPW augmentation term, and it is 0 at π≡1 by construction. Kallus–Mao is a nonparametric result and says nothing about the restricted model. The reported estimator (design-based AIPW) does not attain V_c(D). So P1 bounds a quantity the paper never estimates, and the 'first order' link is asserted without proof.
fatal_flaws.fix: Pick one estimand. Recommended: the primary object is the AIPW design variance, and ρ_j is the admission value. State a proposition that, under the working model with conditional channel information, ρ_j ≈ Σ_c w_c·ΔV_{c,j}/(residual variance) at the planned π, with an explicit remainder. ΔV̂ is then only a screening approximation. Drop the claim that it is the same number.

fatal_flaws.claim: The low-rank structure Θ = Σ u_r⊗v_r⊗w_r shares the candidate factors u_c across gold and rubric channels. Separately, P2's "validity under an arbitrary rubric … no surrogacy assumption" is claimed for the whole framework.
fatal_flaws.problem: A candidate factor shared across channels, scaled only by a channel loading w_k, forces candidate c's effect on channel k to be a fixed linear image of its effect on gold. That is a Prentice/proportional-surrogacy assumption in disguise. It fails exactly when a proposer targets dimension k, which is the surrogate paradox and the planted 'force complete_task by step 20' case. The new candidate moves off the span of the shared factors, so the model is misspecified precisely where the loop pushes. P2's validity holds only for the design-based AIPW. The model-based parts (ΔV screen, KG allocation, posterior keep/drop, corollary (a)) inherit the surrogacy assumption.
fatal_flaws.fix: Add a free candidate×channel main effect β_{ck}, so that candidate means are not transferred across channels. Rubric channels then inform only through the task-varying interaction term Σ u v w. Use the low-rank model only as m̂ inside the AIPW. Make every keep/drop decision from the design-based estimator, not from the model posterior. Report the fitted surrogacy (the shared-loading version) as an ablation.

fatal_flaws.claim: "Tie-aware BTL: P(z_k≠0)=q_{cc′tk} is a discordance nuisance". Also "ψ_c = Σ_t ω_t q_{ct}(2σ(Θ_{ct0}−Θ_{0t0})−1)". Also AIPW is said to allow "transporting effects to families that are never run, such as Validation and sealed".
fatal_flaws.problem: (i) q has one free parameter per (c,c′,t,k) cell, and each cell is observed 1–3 times. That is an incidental-parameter problem. ψ depends directly on q, so the q part of ψ gets no low-rank pooling, and for unrun cells q is unidentified. (ii) The empirical check shows that fixing the seed does not reproduce a run, so paired runs are roughly independent given the task. In that case BTL on sign(Y−Y′) is exactly σ(logit p_c − logit p_c′), with q = p_c(1−p_c′) + p_c′(1−p_c). The 'BTL' is just a reparametrised low-rank logistic (IRT) level model, and treating q as free discards information. (iii) Every family has exactly one task (all 50 prefixes in tasks_challenge50 and val50 are distinct), so v_t for a never-run family is unidentified without task covariates. The 'never run' claim also contradicts the requirement π_ct ≥ π_min > 0.
fatal_flaws.fix: Model levels instead: p_{ctk} = σ(α_{tk} + β_{ck} + Σ_r u_r(c)v_r(t)w_r(k)) for won and for binary checks, and an ordinal or zero-one-inflated link for G. Pairing becomes design blocking (a same-(t,s) random effect). Keep a BTL link only for genuinely pairwise LLM-judge verdicts (OnlineRubrics style); this still reuses the AoS machinery. Restrict ψ to Validation tasks on which the incumbent has been run, and delete the transport-to-sealed claim.

fatal_flaws.claim: "Confirm: cross-fit ρ̂_j, with folds = task families and m̂ fitted on the other folds." Also: "family-cluster bootstrap".
fatal_flaws.problem: Here a family is a single task (50 families with 1 task each). Leave-family-out therefore removes every observation on task t, so v_t cannot be estimated. m̂ for the held-out task reduces to a candidate main effect, and ρ̂_j becomes structurally blind to the task×candidate interaction that the whole method depends on (gate G0). Rubric scores cannot be computed on unrun cells at all, because there is no trajectory. So the only legitimate way a rubric can inform an unrun (c,t) cell is through the incumbent's run on t, or through other candidates' runs on t.
fatal_flaws.fix: Cross-fit at the cell level. Hold out the cells (c,t) with c≠0, and keep the incumbent row (0,t) together with its rubric features in sample. Those features are pre-treatment for candidate c, which makes them legitimate effect-modifier covariates in the CUPED sense and removes the circularity. Cluster standard errors by task. This is also the most promising way for the rubric to pay off: the incumbent's mechanism-level violations on t predict which tasks a mechanism-targeted edit will flip.

fatal_flaws.claim: P2: "ψ̂_c is unbiased … valid CIs for any rubric, including misspecified, gamed or paradoxical ones … cannot push the wrong-keep rate above α". The loop meanwhile runs "while budget left: … keep if P(γ>3pp)≥0.9".
fatal_flaws.problem: Three separate leaks. (a) The rubric D is proposed by an LLM that sees trajectories sampled ∝|e_ct| from the very cells being estimated. D is then admitted using statistics on the same logs, and m̂ uses D. So m̂_ct depends on Y_ct only when R_ct=1, which breaks the predictability assumption and with it AIPW unbiasedness. (b) The screen (ΔV̂ on all data) picks the top 8, and those 8 are then tested on the same data. The p-values used by α-investing are therefore not valid after selection. (c) Continuous monitoring against a fixed 0.9 threshold is optional stopping, so the martingale-CLT fixed-time CIs lose coverage. The rule is also Bayesian while P2 is frequentist.
fatal_flaws.fix: Enforce sequential predictability: D_r and m̂ used for round-r cells may use only data from rounds before r. Screen on one split (e.g. Discovery seed 1) and confirm on another (seed 2 or Validation), or use data fission. Replace the fixed-time CLT with anytime-valid AIPW confidence sequences (Waudby-Smith et al. 2024, time-uniform CLT). Make the keep/drop thresholds the ±3pp decisions from those sequences, and set each α-investing test level to α_j from the wealth rather than a fixed LCB₉₀.

fatal_flaws.claim: E3 gate G3: "A > B on direction IC with P ≥ 0.9, and A ≥ 1.5× D on decisions per pass" (4 arms × 140 passes).
fatal_flaws.problem: (i) 140 passes per arm resolves about 30–45 proposals. Each realized γ has SE of roughly 4–6pp against true effects of 1–7pp, so the reliability of γ is about 0.3–0.5 and any IC is attenuated to about 0.5–0.7× its true value. The difference between two correlations at n≈40 has SE ≈ 0.22. Reaching P≥0.9 for A>B would need an attenuated gap of about 0.3, which the Loop-1 history makes implausible (+2.86pp, CI [−5, +10.7]). (ii) A differs from D in both rubric and allocation. The empirical check says live-task allocation alone could give about 3× savings, so 'A ≥ 1.5×D' can pass with a useless rubric. (iii) This design repeats Loop-1 at similar scale.
fatal_flaws.fix: Drop the online direction-IC headline. Measure direction value offline and interventionally. For M≈10–15 rubric-diagnosed mechanisms, estimate headroom η_k = E[Y(do(fix_k)) − Y] by branching at the violation step with a minimal hint, as a PAV-style prover. Test Spearman(predicted η_k, realized headroom) for the rubric against a token-matched diagnosis. Add an arm 'no rubric + KG/Neyman allocation' to separate the rubric's contribution from allocation. Shift about 300 of the E3 passes into E0/E2 seeds.

fatal_flaws.claim: E2 decision replay: "≥25% fewer passes-to-decision than gold-only uniform at ≤10% wrong-side error … coverage ≥ 0.88 on the planted effects", computed on the E0 corpus (12 candidates × 3 passes).
fatal_flaws.problem: Wrong-side error needs known truth. The non-planted candidates have SE of about 4–6pp from 3 passes, so their truth is unknown. The planted effects are about 16pp, and a large effect like that is easy to resolve under any method. The 3–10pp regime that matters is missing. A replay also cannot run past the corpus horizon: gold-only needs about 3.2 passes for γ=10pp and about 11 for 5pp. So 'passes-to-decision' is censored for exactly the candidates where the claim matters, and with about 4 known-truth candidates the '≤10% wrong-side' figure has no resolution.
fatal_flaws.fix: Build E0 with fewer candidates and more seeds (e.g. 6 real candidates × 6 seeds on Discovery+Validation), and add synthetic planted effects of calibrated size across 3–10pp. Options: step budgets 30/28/26; replacing the agent with the AppWorld oracle solution on a random x% of tasks, which gives exact +γ with heterogeneity; forcing failure on a random x%. Define truth on held-out seeds. Report wrong-side error as a curve over true |γ−δ|.

fatal_flaws.claim: "E1: offline admission (weeks 3–6, 0 passes)" and "rubric step (offline, no GPU)". Budget: "~110 passes per week … Total ≈ 690 passes"; E3 runs weeks 8–14.
fatal_flaws.problem: The E1 pool includes about 45 LLM-judge criteria (20 failure-only, 15 generic, 10 token-matched), plus κ re-judging, the judge-score arm, and the PRM arm. On the local 27B, 45 criteria × 1,800 E0 trajectories × 2 re-judges is about 160k long-context calls, or roughly 1B prefill tokens. That is tens of A800-hours, i.e. many passes' worth of GPU, not 0. 110 passes/week is about 40% of a box shared with a collaborator for 14 straight weeks. E3 ends in week 14 of 16, leaving no slack for crashes (CC_F0_orig already crashed) or for writing. The week-1 default-code fix overlaps the start of E0, so an E0 corpus collected before the harness is frozen is invalid.
fatal_flaws.fix: Make criteria programmatic by default (the LLM writes Python predicates over logs and AppWorld state, so scoring costs nothing). Score all judge criteria in one batched call per trajectory, or use an API model. Freeze the harness, including the default-code fix, before E0. Cut E3 to at most 150 passes total, and finish all experiments by week 12.

fatal_flaws.claim: Gate G0: "a rank-2/3 model beats the additive (candidate + task) model on held-out-seed deviance", with step budgets of 30/25/20 among the 12 E0 candidates.
fatal_flaws.problem: Step-budget candidates mechanically create a rank-1 interaction (budget × steps the task needs; median win at 21–24 steps). G0 will pass because of the planted candidates, not because real harness edits have low-rank interaction structure. The later rubric value then rests on a structure that real edits may lack.
fatal_flaws.fix: Pre-register G0 on the non-planted candidates only, and report the planted-included fit separately. If real edits show only rank 1, restrict the claims to allocation plus incumbent-trajectory effect modifiers.

math_errors: Corollary P1(a), "A channel that loads only on factors gold already identifies (task difficulty, generic 'carefulness') has ΔV = 0", is false under the model as stated. A channel observed independently on a shared, candidate-varying factor gives B_jH_c ≠ 0 and so reduces variance (replication). ΔV=0 holds only for directions that cancel in ψ, such as candidate-invariant task main effects, or for channels that are functions of gold on the same pair, which needs the joint model the framework does not use. The '(formal reason rubric v1/v2 stalled)' also does not follow: v1/v2 failed on direction (dead-hook proposals, TC≈0), not on measurement.

"For a rank-one channel B_j = a_j g_j g_jᵀ, Sherman–Morrison …": a dimension observed on many cells, after profiling out w_j, has Fisher operator rank up to the number of cells. Sherman–Morrison therefore applies per observation. Per dimension the correct formula is Woodbury, ΔV = hᵀA⁻¹U(C⁻¹+UᵀA⁻¹U)⁻¹UᵀA⁻¹h. The algebra of the rank-one formula a⟨g,H⟩²/(1+a⟨g,A⁻¹g⟩) and the iff condition B_jH_c=0 are correct. The 'reliability × alignment² / redundancy' reading for a whole dimension is heuristic.

"Four literatures reduce to one number": partial R² ρ_j and the Gaussian conditional mutual information −½log(1−ρ_j) are equivalent, which is correct. AlphaGen's reward is ΔIC = √R²_{D+j} − √R²_D, which is monotone in ρ_j for fixed D but not equal to it. The Barillas–Shanken α_f²/σ²(ε_f) is an increment in squared Sharpe ratio from a spanning (mean) regression, a different estimand. It relates to R² only through regressing a constant on returns (Britten-Jones), where it gives R²/(1−R²), not ρ_j. So 'equals' is false.

The "Gaussian Garivier–Kaufmann characteristic time (z₀.₉+z_β)²V/|γ−δ|²" is the fixed-sample power formula, not GK. GK gives T*(μ)log(1/δ) with T* = 2σ²/Δ² for a Gaussian threshold test. The numbers do check under the fixed-n formula: 4.51×0.18/0.07² ≈ 166 runs ≈ 3.3 passes. However, V=0.18 comes from a near-replicate pair, so it is a lower bound for genuinely different candidates. 'Admitting j multiplies the dominant sampling term by (1−ρ_j)' applies only to the (1−π)/π augmentation term, not to V_full.

P1(d), 'weakly submodular with ratio ≥ λ_min … greedy is (1−e^{−γ})-optimal': Das–Kempe's ratio uses λ_min of the predictor covariance for linear R² of a single target, evaluated at the population level. With channels correlated at 0.77–0.89 with won, λ_min ≈ 0, so the guarantee is vacuous. The actual admission rule is also a sequential threshold test on the estimate ρ̂, not greedy maximisation of population R².

The VOI formula σ̃ f(−|μ−δ|/σ̃) with f(z)=zΦ(z)+φ(z) is correct for a two-action threshold decision. But σ̃² = ΔV/n_c treats admitting a dimension as buying new data, when it actually re-analyses the same logs. The preposterior variance must therefore be computed on held-out data, or the VOI double-dips.

The admission threshold 'LCB₉₀(ρ̂_j) > τ_a under α-investing wealth' mixes a fixed level of 0.10 with α-investing, whose level α_j for each test is set by the current wealth. Testing only the top 8 after a screen on the same data also makes the p-values invalid after selection.

The rule 'Merge j and k when their loadings have cosine > 0.95 in the A_D⁻¹ metric' does not work at R=2–4. Loadings are 2–4 dimensional, and any two channels dominated by the first factor have cosine near 1, so the rule would collapse distinct dimensions. Use the residual (conditional) correlation of the channel scores instead.

The support for channel 0′ ('power 0.89 vs won 0.77') comes from one planted step-budget cut. That cut specifically removes late wins as G all-or-nothing jumps, a structure that favours sign tests by construction. It is not evidence of a general power advantage.

The ψ over ω_t weights on Validation, with transport to never-run or sealed families, contradicts π_ct ≥ π_min > 0 and is unidentified. With one task per family, v_t and q_ct for an unrun task have no data at all unless there are task-level covariates.
strongest_ideas_to_keep: Value a rubric dimension by targeted (c-optimal) information for the actual decision functional (keep/drop at ±3pp), not by marginal variance (RLER) or log det (Auto-Rubric, D-optimal): ΔV = hᵀ[A⁻¹−(A+B_j)⁻¹]h, which is zero iff B_jH_c=0. This is the natural 'gradient' answer to the user's question, and it sits squarely in the user's AoS framework, provided the per-pair joint (conditional) information fix is applied.

A design-based AIPW with known allocation π ≥ π_min, used as a safety net. Validity then does not depend on rubric quality, and a bad or gamed dimension only widens the CIs. Keep it with sequential predictability and anytime-valid confidence sequences.
Weight evaluation effort by decision relevance: knowledge-gradient/VOI weights φ(|μ−δ|/σ), so runs are not spent on candidates far from ±3pp.

Admit on cross-fit incremental predictive value (partial R² = squared partial IC), with α-investing charged over every proposed dimension, a token-matched control criterion, and hysteresis-based removal re-estimated on the current frontier (Razin et al.). This cleanly answers the 'is a new reward useful' question.

The IC clarification is correct and should be stated to the user plainly. IC's t-statistic equals the slope t-statistic, so IC adds no power by itself. Its value comes from blocking on task difficulty, rank robustness to G's all-or-nothing jumps, and its incremental (partial) form as the admission score. Flat MSE is explained by R²=IC² under Bernoulli noise plus the Clark–West nested-MSPE bias.

Separate measurement value (correlational, ρ_j) from direction value, and estimate direction value interventionally. Headroom via hint-branching at the violation step (a PAV-style prover advantage) is the right mathematical object, and it addresses the surrogate paradox directly. Promote it from one factor in η_k to the primary direction metric.

Rubric features of the incumbent's trajectory on task t, used as pre-treatment effect modifiers for candidate c's effect on t. This is implicit in m̂; make it explicit. It is the one legitimate way a rubric can inform an unrun cell, and it connects 'localize the deficit' with 'predict which tasks a targeted edit flips'.
The planted-paradox candidate (force complete_task early) together with the post-admission drift test on candidates generated after k was admitted. This is a concrete, falsifiable Goodhart check.

Residual-guided criterion proposal with a general→child (edge-case) split when residual mass concentrates on a predicate. This is a natural 'boosting with an LLM weak learner' view of self-evolving rubrics, but residuals must be computed on held-out seeds, or the LLM is asked to explain Bernoulli noise (7 of 9 seed flips are pure completes-vs-runs-out randomness).
overlap_with_prior_work: Jeunen & Ustimenko (KDD 2024, 2402.03915), 'learning metrics that maximise power'; Tripuraneni et al. (KDD 2024, 2309.07893), proxy-metric Sharpe optimisation; Richardson et al. 2023, Pareto-optimal proxy metrics. The measurement side (a composite rubric metric chosen to maximise decision power against a North Star) is essentially this line, applied to harness candidates.
Bibaut, Chou, Ejdemyr, Kallus (KDD 2024, 2402.17637): weak-experiment bias correction via split cross-covariances (JIVE). This is the proposed split-seed de-biasing of ⟨g,H⟩².

Zrnic & Candès (ICML 2024, 2403.03208), active statistical inference; AM-PPI (Brawand et al. 2026, 2605.08429); PPI/PPI++; Kallus & Mao (JRSSB 2025). The AIPW-with-allocation estimator and P2 are standard results from these papers.

Yazdani et al., 'Rubric Rewards from Item Response Theory' (2609.35646, posted 28 Sep 2026): a 2PL model over criterion verdicts, criterion discrimination and difficulty, Fisher-information criterion selection, online EM. This is the nearest competitor; the delta must be targeted (c-optimal) information for a decision functional plus harness-level co-evolution.

Auto-Rubric (Xie et al. 2510.17314): information-gain (coding-rate, D-optimal) criterion selection. RLER/DR Tulu (2511.19399): variance-based rubric retention. OnlineRubrics (2510.07284): criteria elicited from pairwise contrasts. RaR (2507.17746). POW3R (2605.20164): contrast-weighted criteria.

AlphaGen (KDD 2023, 2306.12964): reward = incremental combination-model IC when a factor joins the pool, the same admission logic as ρ_j. R&D-Agent(Q) (NeurIPS 2025): an IC/ICIR-scored hypothesis→code→backtest loop. Feng–Giglio–Xiu (JF 2020): double-selection testing of new factors.

HGM (Wang et al. 2510.21614): clade metaproductivity with Beta–Thompson sampling, reused for η_k. DGM/ADAS/SICA/AlphaEvolve: self-improving agents with fixed evaluators. The 'evaluator co-evolves at the program level' gap is real but narrow.

Frazier, Powell & Dayanik (2009): knowledge gradient. Russo (2020): top-two sampling. Shi et al. (NeurIPS 2024, TRIPLE): best-arm identification for prompt selection. These cover the allocation piece.

Setlur et al. PAV (ICLR 2025, 2410.08146): step reward as advantage under a prover; distinguishability × alignment. This is the conceptual basis of the hint-branching headroom. Razin et al. (NeurIPS 2025, 2503.15477): reward usefulness depends on the policy, which justifies frontier-only re-estimation.

tinyBenchmarks / Fluid / metabench: IRT with Fisher-information item selection. The recommended level model (low-rank logistic) is IRT with candidate×task×channel structure, and reviewers will read it that way.

Athey–Chetty–Imbens–Kang (surrogate index); Prentice (1989); VanderWeele (2013) surrogate paradox. The shared-factor model implicitly assumes surrogacy, and the drift test is a sequential version of known surrogate-validation checks.
verdict:
Major revision; not submittable as written. The core thesis is right, and it is the natural mathematical answer to the user's question. A rubric dimension's value is its targeted information for the loop's actual decision (ΔV = hᵀ[A⁻¹−(A+B)⁻¹]h, zero iff it is orthogonal to the least-favourable direction). A design-based AIPW with known allocation keeps inference valid whatever the rubric does. The IC intuition reduces to blocking, rank robustness and partial (incremental) IC, and the framework states this correctly.

The framework currently welds two incompatible estimands. One is a model-based low-rank efficiency gain (P1). The other is a design-based AIPW variance reduction (ρ, P2). Four modelling choices then break the link between them:
- (i) channels computed on the same trajectory are treated as independent Fisher sources, so near-copies of won dominate the screen;
- (ii) a shared candidate factor across channels is a hidden surrogacy assumption, and it fails exactly where the proposer optimises;
- (iii) tie-aware BTL with a free q per cell is an incidental-nuisance reparametrisation of a low-rank logistic model, and it makes transport unidentified;
- (iv) leave-family-out cross-fitting, with one task per family, zeroes out the task×candidate interaction the method relies on.

P2's 'valid for any rubric' is also broken in practice. Rubric selection leaks the estimated cells into m̂, the same data is screened and then tested, and optional stopping runs against a 0.9 posterior threshold.

The experiments are also mis-sized. E2 lacks ground truth in the 3–10pp regime, and the replay is censored at 3 passes. E3's direction-IC gate is underpowered: about 40 proposals, noise-attenuated, compared across arms. It also confounds the rubric with allocation.

Minimal path to an ICML-credible paper in 16 weeks:
1. Switch to a low-rank logistic/ordinal level model with free candidate×channel main effects. Use BTL only for pairwise judge channels. Compute channel information conditional on gold for each pair.
2. Make ρ_j (cell-level cross-fit, keeping the incumbent row and its rubric features as pre-treatment effect modifiers) the estimand. Present ΔV as its provable first-order approximation under the working model.
3. Enforce sequential predictability and split screen from confirm. Use anytime-valid AIPW confidence sequences for keep/drop.
4. Re-scope the empirical claim to measurement plus allocation, using an E0 with more seeds and calibrated planted effects of 3–10pp (oracle-solution or forced-failure injection).
5. Measure direction value offline, as interventional headroom via hint-branching against a token-matched diagnosis, instead of an online 560-pass loop.
6. Default to programmatic criteria so that 'offline' really costs 0 GPU.

With these changes the novelty is moderate but defensible against Yazdani et al. (IRT rubric) and Jeunen & Ustimenko (power-maximising metrics). The differentiators are decision-targeted c-optimal criterion value, surrogacy-robust design-based validity, and evaluator co-evolution at the program level. The fit with the user's semiparametric and low-rank expertise is excellent. As written, the capability-improvement headline ('reward drives self-evolution') is not supported by any powered experiment and should not be claimed.
